text:
li: Heads-up — saw a weird perf delta on qwen-7b-v2 with the FP8 KV cache enabled. 98th p50 tail up ~12% on short-chat workload. anyone else seeing this?
anya: saw the alert in dashboards, digging now. can you paste the exact commit/seed?
matt: pinging infra-bot for recent rollout info. maybe a kernel selection change rolled out?
li: commit a2f3b0f -> kernel-router heuristics updated to prefer matmul-low-latency kernels at seq<=64. repro run: `perf run --model=qwen-7b-v2 --kernel-router=canary --kv-cache=fp8 --batching=auto --workload=short-chat`
perf-bot: quick summary from perf cluster: 
```
model: qwen-7b-v2
cfg: fp8-kv, canary-kernels, batching=auto
requests: 50k
latency p50/p95/p99: 12ms / 48ms / 120ms
baseline: 10.8ms / 44ms / 110ms
regression: +11.1% p50, +9% p95
```
li: repro log shows more KV eviction churn when heads mismatch occurs (mixed head dims during sharded loading). eviction spikes at token 8-12 prefixes.
nisha: interesting — could be our demotion policy interacting with FP8 quantization rounding. when keys have uneven magnitude the quantizer crosses a threshold and we evict more aggressively.
anya: can you dump a sample of KV norms and quantization scales? a small csv is fine.
li: attaching snippet: `kv_norms.csv` (excerpt) - values cluster into two modes: ~0.9 and ~0.03. quant scale per-row: [0.98, 0.95, 0.12, 0.11, ...]
matt: that bimodal distribution smells like mixed attention head layout (some heads offloaded to different kernels or padded). kernel-router might be sharding heads across different execution kernels causing scale divergence.
infra-bot: detected recent rollout: kernel-router:v3 -> promoted to canary across 12% of capacity at 2026-11-21T03:12Z.
li: experiment idea: try prefix-aware demotion where we avoid demoting rows with high variance in norm across head groups. quick patch: set `kv.eviction.pref_threshold = 0.2` and `kv.quantize.per_row_scale = true`
anya: small A/B planned: route 10% traffic to config (A) per_row_scale + demotion_tweak and (B) keep current. will run 4h.
perf-bot: started A/B job 1803456795-A_B_kv_fp8 -> collecting latency + token-cost + cache-hit-rate
li: also profiling scheduler for micro-batch choices. noticed batching heuristics prefer larger batches on cold prefixes which increases seq reuse but also increases prefix-cache pressure. patching `batcher.max_seq_for_agg` from 64->48 for canary to reduce simultaneous prefixes.
nisha: curious about quality impact — per_row_scale might change logits slightly, run the regen check on the eval prompt set.
matt: running eval set now; no substantive delta on BLEU/QA-type metrics (tiny 0.2% change in avg top1).
li: interim results from A/B after 2h: A (per_row_scale + demotion tweak): p50 -2.5% vs B: +10% regression. cache hit-rate A: 87% vs B: 74%. cost per token A: -3%.
anya: looks promising. two open items: confirm no long-tail p99 regressions, and validate memory overhead of per_row_scale (we add ~3% metadata).
perf-bot: A/B job finalizing, p99 shows slight improvement -4% for A.
li: plan: roll per_row_scale + prefix-aware demotion to canary@20% and monitor 24h. also add telemetry to surface per-head scale variance so we can alert before eviction churn.
matt: will prep rollout PR and add automated regression gates in pipeline: block if p50 regresses >5% or cache-hit drop >6%.
anya: thanks team — nice catch. filing follow-up ticket with root cause notes + reproduction steps and linking perf-run id (1803456795). :thumbsup:
infra-bot: rollout scheduled for 2026-11-21T08:00Z (canary 20%). monitoring channel: #eng-runtime-alerts
li: leaving this thread — will update with final metrics once 24h completes. thanks!
